newsitem.title: FRANCE: Global LNG supply to grow but European buyers wary.
newsitem.headline: Global LNG supply to grow but European buyers wary.

text.p: Exports of liquefied natural gas (LNG) are set to grow by 25 percent or more in the next few years as a range of new projects come onstream, a conference heard on Friday.

Tony Hanna, chief excutive of Oman LNG, said he estimated global LNG supply now at 90 to 100 million tonnes a year, but projects recently completed, under construction or in planning in Abu Dhabi, Malaysia, Brunei, Nigeria, Trinidad, Yemen, Oman and elsewhere would raise this by a quarter or more.
LNG is in greatest demand in the Far East, especially South Korea.
Pierre Boutelant, director of gas at Yemen LNG Company, which is only in the planning stages, said the project was unlikely to start unless they secure a contract with a Korean buyer.
But for Europe, which is well supplied with natural gas, LNG has few attractions.
Jean Vermeire, director of Belgium's Distrigaz, said Belgium had a theoretical advantage in having an LNG terminal at Antwerp.
But he added: "LNG had an advantage in the past in power generation in that it could give you very quick bursts of capacity at times of peak demand.

"But with more combined cycle power stations, you can build a gas oil storage unit with five or 10 days supply next to a power station. Then you can install capacity right in the middle of the grid, not at the coast."
He added that with the loss of this advantage, LNG was unlikely to compete with pipeline gas on cost. --Sebastian Alison
